properties.natural_language: Before processing any NewPooledTransactionHashes (0x08) announcement metadata, the node MUST treat all announced fields (hash, type, size, address, nonce) as UNVERIFIED and use them only as optimization hints for request prioritization, never for security decisions such as access control or rate limiting by sender.

After retrieving a full transaction via GetPooledTransactions, the node MUST validate that the announced metadata (hash, type, size, address, nonce) matches the actual transaction fields. If any field differs, the announcing peer MUST be flagged as a protocol violator and penalized.

The system MUST NEVER use unverified sender addresses from transaction announcements to filter or censor transactions. Filtering based on announced sender addresses constitutes a censorship path that violates protocol neutrality. Only request priority may be affected by unverified metadata.

Before accepting a block from any P2P peer for state transition processing, the node MUST fully validate the block header, proof-of-work/proof-of-stake, all transactions, and state transitions. Block size may be larger due to cheaper calldata (EIP-2028) but propagation delays must not exceed security bounds.

Before accepting a transaction submitted via JSON-RPC, the node MUST validate: intrinsic gas covers calldata costs (16 gas per non-zero byte, 4 per zero byte per EIP-2028), blob count does not exceed 6 (EIP-7594), cell proofs are batch-verified against KZG commitments, and versioned hashes match commitments.

After receiving column samples from DAS custodian peers, ALL received column samples MUST have their KZG proofs batch-verified against known commitments. Insufficient valid samples MUST indicate data withholding. Data availability requires at least 50% of columns for reconstruction.

Before aggregating sync committee messages, the aggregator MUST verify that all collected sync committee messages are signature-verified and that beacon_block_root matches block.parent_root for consistency. The best contribution MUST be selected by highest signature count per subnet.

Before accepting a block from a block producer via P2P, the node MUST validate against the correct consensus ruleset based on block number. For EIP-1588, blocks at or above block 7280000 MUST be validated with ProgPoW rules; blocks below with pre-fork rules. PoW verification MUST use the appropriate algorithm for the fork state.

Before deploying any contract, EOF containers MUST pass full structural validation (magic bytes 0xEF00, header, type/code/data sections), code validation (valid opcodes per EIP-3670), and static stack analysis (no underflow below 0, no overflow above 1024, per EIP-5450). Both initcode and deployed code MUST be independently validated.

Before the CL validator includes an execution payload in a beacon block, the Engine API channel MUST be JWT-authenticated. Fork choice updates sent via engine_forkchoiceUpdated MUST include valid safe and finalized block hashes. If the execution engine returns SYNCING status, the validator MUST NOT propose a block.

After the execution engine returns an execution payload via engine_getPayload, the CL validator MUST verify the payload is structurally valid and fits within beacon block constraints. A compromised execution engine could return invalid payloads, so content validation is required despite JWT authentication.

Before attesting to any received beacon block, the validator MUST pass both beacon state transition validation AND execution payload validation via the Engine API. Invalid blocks received from CL gossip peers MUST be rejected and peers sending invalid data SHOULD be penalized.

The node ID used for PeerDAS custody column assignment MUST NOT be easily manipulable by attackers. Custody column assignment MUST be deterministic based on node ID, ensuring attackers cannot generate node IDs to concentrate custody of specific columns for targeted data withholding.

Blob transactions MUST contain exactly matching quantities of versioned hashes, blobs, and commitments. Cell proofs count MUST equal CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB * len(blobs). Any mismatch MUST result in transaction rejection.

After KZG commitment hash validation, cell proofs MUST be batch-verified against computed extension cells. Transactions with invalid proofs MUST be rejected to prevent invalid blobs from entering the mempool.

Before the node considers data available for a slot, it MUST establish a diverse peer set for required custody columns and perform pseudorandomized sampling. Peer discovery MUST ensure connections to peers custodying different columns to prevent eclipse attacks.

After data reconstruction from partial columns, at least 50% of all columns MUST have been acquired with valid KZG proofs before erasure code reconstruction can proceed. If fewer than 50% of valid columns are available, reconstruction MUST fail and data MUST be reported as unavailable.

Sync committee message production MUST occur at the 1/3 slot mark. Contribution aggregation MUST occur at the 2/3 slot mark. These timing deadlines are critical: clock skew causing missed deadlines reduces participation rates and weakens light client security guarantees.

The sync committee aggregator selection MUST use a cryptographic selection proof via is_sync_committee_aggregator targeting approximately 16 aggregators per subcommittee. Selection MUST be deterministic based on validator key and slot, preventing manipulation of aggregator assignment.

The sync committee message lifecycle MUST follow the sequence: validator assigned -> join subnet -> produce message -> check aggregator eligibility -> aggregate (if selected) -> proposer collects -> include in block. Subnet subscription MUST occur with a random offset of 1-4 epochs before the period ends to avoid thundering herd.

Before executing any I/O-intensive opcode after the Tangerine Whistle fork, the EVM MUST apply the increased gas costs (CALL: 700, BALANCE: 400, EXTCODESIZE/EXTCODECOPY: 700, SLOAD: 200, SELFDESTRUCT: 5000). Insufficient gas MUST trigger an out-of-gas exception before the operation executes.

For CALL/DELEGATECALL/CALLCODE operations, the gas forwarded to the child context MUST be capped at min(requested_gas, available_gas - available_gas/64) per the 63/64 rule (EIP-150). This ensures the caller always retains at least 1/64 of gas for post-call handling and prevents deep call stack attacks.

Before executing SELFDESTRUCT, the system MUST check whether the beneficiary account exists. Base gas of 5000 MUST always be charged. If the beneficiary is a new account, an additional 25000 gas MUST be charged for account creation. Insufficient gas MUST prevent the operation.

Calldata gas pricing MUST charge exactly 4 gas per zero byte and 16 gas per non-zero byte (reduced from 68 per EIP-2028). The intrinsic gas of a transaction MUST include base cost plus the sum of all calldata byte costs. Transactions with gas limit below intrinsic gas MUST be rejected.

After calculating intrinsic gas, the transaction gas limit MUST be compared against the intrinsic gas requirement. Transactions with gas limit >= intrinsic gas proceed to execution; transactions with gas limit < intrinsic gas MUST be rejected without execution.

Block propagation delay MUST remain within acceptable security bounds per the Sompolinsky-Zohar model (beta/lambda >= 1/(1+D*lambda)). Reduced calldata gas costs (EIP-2028) enable larger blocks; malicious block producers MUST NOT be able to exploit cheap calldata to create blocks that propagate slowly enough to gain selfish mining advantage.

EOF validation MUST reject any container where static stack analysis detects potential underflow (pop from empty stack) or overflow (stack exceeds 1024 items) on any execution path. This eliminates runtime stack errors by catching them at deploy time.

EOF function calls via CALLF MUST push the return address to the internal return stack before entering the called section. RETF MUST pop and use the return address to resume the caller. JUMPF (tail call) MUST transfer execution without pushing a return address. The return stack MUST maintain LIFO ordering.

After EOF contract creation, both initcode and deployed code MUST have passed full EOF validation. If initcode is invalid, creation MUST fail before execution. If initcode executes successfully but generates invalid deployed code, creation MUST also fail. No invalid EOF bytecode may be stored on-chain.

Before the ProgPoW fork activation at block 7280000 (EIP-1588), all nodes MUST have upgraded to support the new consensus rules. Failure to upgrade results in a chain split between upgraded and non-upgraded nodes at the fork block.

After block validation under EIP-1588 rules, blocks MUST have their proof of work verified against the correct algorithm (pre-fork or ProgPoW). Blocks passing PoW verification are deemed valid; blocks failing verification MUST be rejected.

The Bellatrix validator block proposal MUST follow the two-step process: first call engine_forkchoiceUpdated to receive payload_id, then call engine_getPayload to retrieve the built payload. Post-merge proposals use the latest execution payload header as parent; pre-merge proposals use the terminal PoW block.

Before applying Osaka fork state transitions, the system MUST verify that all previous fork rules (through Prague) are correctly implemented and activated. Missing or incorrect prior fork implementations would cause consensus failures.

The Osaka block processing pipeline MUST follow the sequence: validate block structure -> process transactions -> update state trie -> process protocol requests. Blocks failing structural validation MUST be rejected before transaction execution begins.

After detecting an exception during Osaka block processing, all partial state changes MUST be rolled back to the pre-operation snapshot. The error MUST be propagated to the caller. No partial state modifications may persist after a failed operation.

EVM memory MUST be initialized as an empty bytearray at the start of each execution context. Memory expansion gas MUST be charged BEFORE the write operation occurs. Uninitialized memory MUST NOT leak data between transactions or contract calls.

Buffer reads that extend beyond the buffer boundary MUST return zero-padded data for out-of-bounds bytes. Reads fully within bounds return the buffer slice directly. This prevents information leakage from adjacent memory.

Before executing any memory operation requiring expansion, the system MUST calculate whether expansion is needed and charge the quadratic memory expansion gas cost. If gas is insufficient for expansion, an out-of-gas exception MUST be raised before the memory operation proceeds.

Memory read operations on allocated memory MUST return the exact bytes previously written at the specified position. The memory model MUST be byte-addressable with U256 positions, though practical limits are enforced via quadratic gas costs making very large positions economically infeasible.

The Osaka fork state transition MUST complete successfully for a block to be considered executed. The state transition function MUST process all transactions under Osaka rules and produce the correct post-state root.

Before announcing a transaction to peers, the node MUST build the NewPooledTransactionHashes message with all required fields: hash, type, size, source address, and nonce. The 0x08 message format MUST be used.

After receiving a transaction announcement, the node MUST parse the metadata and check pool interest using the nonce and address hints. Transactions deemed interesting (filling mempool gaps or providing value) MUST be requested via GetPooledTransactions; those deemed not interesting MAY be skipped.

Blob transaction gossip MUST use wrapper_version=1 format including cell_proofs. The transaction sender MUST compute cell KZG proofs for all blob cells including extensions before gossip. This outsources proof computation from block producers to transaction senders.

After requesting missing columns from peer custodians, if the node receives sufficient valid columns (>=50%), erasure code reconstruction MUST recover the full data matrix. The reconstructed data MUST be verifiable against the original KZG commitments.

EOF containers with magic bytes 0xEF00 MUST be routed to EOF validation. Bytecode without the EOF prefix MUST be treated as legacy format. This bifurcation ensures no legacy bytecode is incorrectly subjected to EOF validation rules and vice versa.

Invalid EOF containers MUST be rejected at deploy time. Structure-invalid containers MUST fail before code validation. Code-invalid containers MUST fail before stack validation. No invalid EOF bytecode may reach the deployed state.

After metadata validation, if all announced fields match the actual transaction, the transaction proceeds normally. If metadata matches, no peer penalty is applied. This positive path ensures honest peers are not penalized.

The hint-applied state for announcement metadata MUST only affect request prioritization (which transactions to fetch first), never whether a transaction is fetched at all. Optimization hints from unverified data MUST NOT result in complete exclusion of any announced transactions.

Before a blob transaction with count exceeding 6 blobs proceeds to further validation, the blob count check MUST reject it. The maximum of 6 blobs per transaction is a hard limit that MUST be enforced before any proof verification occurs.

I/O operation execution in the Tangerine Whistle fork MUST only proceed after gas has been deducted and confirmed sufficient. The operation MUST complete atomically - either fully executing after gas deduction or not executing at all if gas is insufficient.

Before a validator assigned to a slot can propose a beacon block with an execution payload, the terminal PoW block MUST be detected (pre-merge) via terminal total difficulty or override hash. Post-merge, the latest execution payload header is used as parent.

Block validation under EIP-1588 MUST first determine the active ruleset by checking the block number against the activation threshold (7280000) before proceeding to PoW verification. The ruleset determination MUST be deterministic and consistent across all validating nodes.

Before the Osaka fork state transition processes a block, the fork activation criteria MUST have been met. Blocks processed under Osaka rules MUST have entered through the activation check gate, ensuring no pre-fork blocks are processed with post-fork rules.
